title: mk_binary_internal's error message indexes the second value array with the first array's index, so a failing operation past the shorter array's end reads off its pdata
object: fv2->pdata, one direct g_malloc'd pointer array inside a GPtrArray
lifetime_ender: NONE -- both arrays are alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: two independent indices over two arrays of independent lengths: the working call uses fv2->pdata[j] correctly, and the error message three lines later uses fv2->pdata[i], where i indexes fv1. Whenever fv1 is longer than fv2 and the operation fails past fv2's end, the read leaves fv2->pdata.
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: a GPtrArray's pdata is one direct g_malloc, grown with g_realloc, and nothing sub-allocates it. Under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED.
nested_why: nothing sub-allocated the crossed region: a GPtrArray's pdata is one direct g_malloc, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. The platform's malloc/free; GLib is not linked, and g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure, which is all this case uses of it (corpus.h states that for the corpus). The two arrays are 4 and 2 entries -- the asymmetry IS the defect's premise, and the case asserts both that the error path's index is past fv2 and that the working call's index is not, so a reduction that lost the asymmetry fails rather than reporting a verdict. func() and debug_op_error are reduced to the read each performs; nothing about WHICH index is used is reduced, because that is the defect.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source, keyed on the full expression so it cannot match the correct call: v4.6.8:epan/dfilter/dfvm.c contains `debug_op_error(fv1->pdata[i], fv2->pdata[i]` 1 time and the fixed `...fv2->pdata[j]` 0 times. Two-sided. LIVE AT THE PIN.
distinguishing: the defect is on the ERROR PATH ONLY, and the correct index is three lines above it in the same statement block -- which is why it survived review and why a reduction exercising the success path would report a clean result and learn nothing. This corpus's case 0 crosses on the main path with an attacker-chosen magnitude; this one crosses only when the operation fails, by exactly the difference in the two arrays' lengths. The crossed value is merely formatted into a debug string, so `damage` is 0: a consequence-based test cannot see this defect at all, while a bounds check sees the read. That is the same asymmetry ffmpeg/plain-heap-repros case 1 records, and it is the reason both rows exist.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle:
MEASURED 2026-10-07, results/20261007-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT**, confirming this arm's prediction AND the size-class condition it stated. signal=34 (SIGPROT), si_code=1 (BOUNDS), fault at 0x102416, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x102406` from the ELF independently -- the fault lies INSIDE the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, so the range is the criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. fv2->pdata is malloc(16), 16 is a size class with zero slack, and the read at index 3 is byte offset 24, so the crossing leaves the USABLE allocation. 6 of 6 arms, runner exit 0, both platform controls firing in the same boot.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 in the same vehicle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x10243e, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x10242e` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
